stem:
Xavier asks why a circle is a special limiting case for line symmetry and rotational symmetry.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Say the circle matches itself after some turn, but skip that the turn is about the centre and that every diameter is a symmetry line.
Say the centre is what the circle creates, instead of using the centre to test turns and diameters.
A circle matches itself after a turn by any angle about its centre, and every diameter is a line of symmetry, so it has infinitely many rotational symmetries and infinitely many symmetry lines.
Require group-theory language about symmetry groups, beyond line and turn matching for the circle.

teacher.key_rationale: A circle is invariant under any rotation about its centre and under reflection in every diameter, so both kinds of symmetry occur infinitely often.
